In [[geometry]], this polyhedron can be seen as either a polyhedral [[stellation]] or a [[Polyhedron compound|compound]].

== As a compound ==

It can be seen as the [[Polyhedron compound|compound]] of an [[icosahedron]] and [[dodecahedron]]. It is one of four compounds constructed from a [[Platonic solid]] or [[Kepler-Poinsot solid]], and its [[Dual polyhedron|dual]].

It has [[icosahedral symmetry]] ('''I'''<sub>''h''</sub>) and the same [[vertex arrangement]] as a [[rhombic triacontahedron]].

This can be seen as the three-dimensional equivalent of the compound of two pentagons ({10/2} "[[decagram (geometry)|decagram]]"); this series continues into the fourth dimension as the [[compound of 120-cell and 600-cell]] and into higher dimensions as compounds of hyperbolic tilings.

== As a stellation ==

This [[polyhedron]] is the first [[stellation]] of the [[icosidodecahedron]], and given as [[List of Wenninger polyhedron models#Stellations of icosidodecahedron|Wenninger model index 47]].

The stellation facets for construction are:
:[[Image:First stellation of icosidodecahedron facets.png|300px]][[Image:First stellation of icosidodecahedron pentfacets.png|300px]][[File:First stellation of icosidodecahedron.png|280px]]

== As a Faceting ==
The compound of a Dodecahedron and an Icosahedron shares the same vertices as a list of other polyhedra, including the [[Rhombic triacontahedron]] and the [[Small triambic icosahedron]].

== In popular culture ==
In the film ''[[Tron]]'' (1982), the character [[List of Tron (franchise) characters#Bit|Bit]] took this shape when not speaking.

In the cartoon series ''[[Steven Universe]]'' (2013-2019), [[List of Steven Universe characters#Steven Universe|Steven]]'s shield bubble, briefly used in the episode [[Change Your Mind (Steven Universe)|Change Your Mind]], had this shape.
